scientific_scope_status: Dual-rail loss provides a known erasure sector, and the 2026 cavity SWS CZ is positive prior evidence. Loss during its coupler-target cross-Kerr can leave a correlated unknown partial phase even when a final erasure flag is known. The proposed coupler-inclusive monitor requires about an 8 ns event-time uncertainty for a stated small-angle phase-error budget whose infidelity contribution is quadratic in residual phase; the cited continuous-monitor experiment used a much longer integration window on a different transmon platform and does not demonstrate that timing for the SWS cavity path. Which-path dephasing, monitor-induced loss/backaction, full-circuit performance and matched cost remain open. Credit primary experimental authors; no new capability or quantum advantage is claimed.
